title: Input & Output — Talking to the User
description: Make programs that ask questions and show answers.

sections.content:
So far, all our programs have used fixed values — we wrote the data directly in the code. Real programs talk to the user: they ask questions and respond to answers.

In Python, `input()` pauses the program and waits for the user to type something. Whatever the user types is returned as a string.

sections.code:
name = input("What is your name? ")
print("Hello, " + name + "!")
sections.explanation: input() shows the question in the brackets, then waits. The user types their answer and presses Enter. Their answer is stored in name and used in print().

sections.content:
Remember: `input()` always returns a string — even if the user types a number.

If you want to do math with user input, you must convert it first using `int()` or `float()`.

sections.code:
age_text = input("How old are you? ")
age = int(age_text)        # convert to number
next_year = age + 1
print("Next year you will be " + str(next_year))
sections.explanation: Step 1: get the input (always a string). Step 2: convert it to int. Step 3: do math. Step 4: convert back to string for printing.

sections.question: What type does input() always return?
options: It depends on what the user types
sections.explanation: input() always returns a str (string), no matter what the user types. You must convert it yourself if you need a number.

sections.content: You can also print formatted messages using an f-string. An f-string starts with the letter `f` before the quotes. Inside, you put variable names in curly braces `{}` and Python fills them in automatically.

sections.code:
name = "Htike"
age = 17
city = "Mandalay"

print(f"My name is {name}. I am {age} years old and I live in {city}.")
sections.explanation: f-strings are easier than using + to join everything. Python replaces {name}, {age}, {city} with the actual values.

sections.prompt: Write a program that asks for the user's name and age. Then print: "[name] is [age] years old and will be [age+1] next year." Use an f-string.
sections.starterCode:
# Ask for name
# Ask for age (remember to convert!)
# Print the sentence
sections.hint: name = input("...")  then  age = int(input("..."))  then  print(f"...{name}...{age}...{age+1}...")
sections.solution:
name = input("What is your name? ")
age = int(input("How old are you? "))
print(f"{name} is {age} years old and will be {age + 1} next year.")
